items.title: Spring festival, social practices of the Chinese people in celebration of traditional new year
items.quote_en: In China, the spring festival marks the beginning of the new year... involves a variety of social practices to usher in the new year, pray for good fortune, celebrate family reunions and promote community harmony. The spring festival promotes family values, social cohesion and peace while providing a sense of identity and continuity for the Chinese people.
items.quote_cn: 春节是中国传统新年，包含辞旧迎新、祈福、家庭团圆与社区和谐等社会实践；传承家庭价值与社会认同。
items.statement_for_kb: UNESCO inscribed China's Spring Festival social practices on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2024, highlighting family reunion, community harmony and cultural continuity.
items._pack_desc: 官方与国际组织：美食 / 非遗 / CGTN

items.theme: CGTN on Spring Festival UNESCO recognition
items.title: Spring Festival, a celebration shared with the world
items.quote_en: In 2024, the Spring Festival, marking the social practices of the Chinese people in celebration of the traditional Chinese New Year, was officially inscribed on the UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
items.quote_cn: 2024年，春节相关社会实践被列入联合国教科文组织人类非物质文化遗产代表作名录。
items.statement_for_kb: CGTN reports that Spring Festival social practices were inscribed on UNESCO's ICH Representative List in 2024 and are increasingly shared worldwide.
items._pack_desc: 官方与国际组织：美食 / 非遗 / CGTN

items.title: Traditional tea processing techniques and associated social practices in China
items.quote_en: Tea is ubiquitous in the Chinese people's daily life and is served steeped or boiled in homes, workplaces, tea houses, restaurants and temples. It is an important part of socialization and of ceremonies such as weddings and sacrifices.
items.quote_cn: 茶贯穿中国人日常生活，见于家庭、职场、茶馆、餐馆与寺庙；也是社交与婚嫁、祭祀等仪式的重要媒介。
items.statement_for_kb: UNESCO recognizes China's traditional tea processing techniques and social practices (2022); tea producers developed six main tea categories plus reprocessed teas, with over 2,000 products.
items._pack_desc: 官方与国际组织：美食 / 非遗 / CGTN

items.theme: CGTN on Chinese tea UNESCO listing
items.title: Chinese tea making joins UNESCO list
items.quote_en: Traditional tea processing techniques and their associated social practices in China were added to UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity... tea producers have developed six categories of tea: green, yellow, dark, white, oolong and black teas.
items.quote_cn: 中国传统制茶技艺及其相关社会实践列入非遗名录；六大茶类：绿、黄、黑（暗茶）、白、青（乌龙）、红茶。
items.statement_for_kb: CGTN: China's traditional tea-making and associated social practices joined UNESCO's ICH list; six tea categories plus flower-scented and other reprocessed teas.
items._pack_desc: 官方与国际组织：美食 / 非遗 / CGTN

items.title: Chinese paper-cut
items.quote_en: Present throughout China and in various ethnic groups, paper-cut is a popular art integral to everyday lives... As a key part of Chinese social life in all ethnic groups, paper-cut expresses the moral principles, philosophies and aesthetic ideals of its exponents.
items.quote_cn: 剪纸流行于中国各民族日常生活，用于装饰、节庆与祈愿，表达道德观念与审美理想。
items.statement_for_kb: Chinese paper-cutting (inscribed 2009) is a widely practiced folk art across ethnic groups, used in decor, festivals and ritual contexts.
items._pack_desc: 官方与国际组织：美食 / 非遗 / CGTN

items.title: Peking opera
items.quote_en: Peking opera is a performance art incorporating singing, reciting, acting, martial arts... They tell stories of history, politics, society and daily life and aspire to inform as they entertain.
items.quote_cn: 京剧融合唱、念、做、打，以北京、天津、上海等地为表演中心，讲述历史与社会生活故事。
items.statement_for_kb: Peking opera (inscribed 2010) combines singing, reciting, acting and martial arts; it remains a widely recognized element of China's cultural heritage.
items._pack_desc: 官方与国际组织：美食 / 非遗 / CGTN

items.title: Chinese calligraphy
items.quote_en: Chinese calligraphy has always been more than simply a tool for communication, incorporating as it does the element of artistry... In its distinctive Chinese form, calligraphy offers an important channel for the appreciation of traditional culture and for arts education.
items.quote_cn: 书法不仅是书写工具，更是艺术；五种书体（篆、隶、草、行、楷）仍用于教育与文化认同。
items.statement_for_kb: Chinese calligraphy (inscribed 2009) is both communication and artistry, using seal, official, cursive, running and regular scripts; it remains central to cultural education and identity.
items._pack_desc: 官方与国际组织：美食 / 非遗 / CGTN

items.title: Uyghur Muqam of Xinjiang
items.quote_en: Throughout its history, the Xinjiang region has been marked by a high degree of cultural exchange between East and West, due in large part to its central location along the Silk Road. Xinjiang Uyghur Muqam includes songs, dances, folk and classical music.
items.quote_cn: 新疆地处丝绸之路，历史上东西文化交流频繁；维吾尔木卡姆包含歌曲、舞蹈、民间与古典音乐。
items.statement_for_kb: The Uyghur Muqam of Xinjiang (inscribed 2008) is a suite of songs, dances and music reflecting Silk Road cultural exchange and Uyghur social life.
items._pack_desc: 官方与国际组织：美食 / 非遗 / CGTN

items.title: Traditional handicrafts of making Xuan paper
items.quote_en: Handmade from the tough bark of the Tara Wing-Celtis or Blue Sandalwood tree and rice straw, Xuan paper is known for its strong, smooth surface, its ability to absorb water and moisten ink... It has been widely used in calligraphy, painting and book printing.
items.quote_cn: 宣纸以青檀皮与稻草等手工制作，吸墨适中，广泛用于书法、绘画与印刷。
items.statement_for_kb: Traditional Xuan paper making (inscribed 2009) in Jing County, Anhui supports calligraphy and painting; the handcraft process involves more than a hundred steps.
items._pack_desc: 官方与国际组织：美食 / 非遗 / CGTN

items.title: China - UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (state page)
items.quote_en: Official UNESCO country page listing China's inscribed intangible cultural heritage elements (including Spring Festival 2024, tea 2022, Peking opera, calligraphy, paper-cut, Uyghur Muqam, etc.).
items.quote_cn: 联合国教科文组织中国非遗名录总览页，可核对各项入选年份与条目。
items.statement_for_kb: UNESCO's China ICH state page is the authoritative index of inscribed Chinese intangible heritage elements used for story-type grounding.
items._pack_desc: 官方与国际组织：美食 / 非遗 / CGTN

items.theme: Xi'an Silk Road city welcome culture (third-party)
items.title: The Eastern promise of Xi'an
items.quote_en: Famed for being the eastern terminus of the Silk Road... Xi'an was usually the first port of call for visitors to the East, and has a long tradition of welcoming guests from across the globe.
items.quote_cn: 西安作为丝绸之路东端，长期接待来自全球的访客，具有开放迎客传统。
items.statement_for_kb: BBC Travel describes Xi'an as the eastern terminus of the Silk Road with a long tradition of welcoming international visitors; local food (dumplings, hotpot) is part of the city experience.
items._pack_desc: 官方与国际组织：美食 / 非遗 / CGTN

items.title: Silk Roads: the Routes Network of Chang'an-Tianshan Corridor
items.quote_en: This property is a 5,000 km section of the extensive Silk Roads network, stretching from Chang'an/Luoyang... to the Zhetysu region of Central Asia... linking multiple civilizations and facilitating far-reaching exchanges of activities in trade, religious beliefs, scientific knowledge, technological innovation, cultural practices and the arts.
items.quote_cn: 丝绸之路：长安—天山廊道（约5000公里）连接多文明，促进贸易、信仰、科技与文化交流。
items.statement_for_kb: UNESCO's Silk Roads Chang'an-Tianshan Corridor (inscribed 2014) spans about 5,000 km from Chang'an/Luoyang into Central Asia and documents long-distance exchange of trade, beliefs, knowledge and arts.
items._pack_desc: 日常生活 / 语言 / 体育 / 妇女 / 城市

items.theme: Travel breaks stereotypes about the world
items.creator: Mike Chen
items.title: Mike Chen talks food, YouTube and traveling the world
items.quote_en: That was when I first realized I wanted to get out there and see the world because it's not at all what you hear about from other people.
items.quote_cn: Chen：亲身旅行后发现世界并不像别人转述的那样，想走出去亲眼看。
items.statement_for_kb: Mike Chen tells US students that firsthand travel showed him the world is not what secondhand stories suggest—an openness frame useful for culture storytelling.
items._pack_desc: 海外网站洋网红 / 外籍创作者图文

items.theme: Guardian: Dunlop matchmakes Westerners with Chinese food
items.creator: Fuchsia Dunlop
items.title: I eat to understand: cook and writer Fuchsia Dunlop on her lifelong love of Chinese cuisine
items.quote_en: Dunlop... loves nothing more than matchmaking Western eaters with what is to them unfamiliar and sometimes intimidating Chinese food. In 30 years of exploring and documenting the country, she has done for China what Elizabeth David did for Mediterranean food... When I go to China, people ask me, 'Why have you come to China?' And I say, 'I've come to eat.'
items.quote_cn: 卫报：Dunlop 30年来向西方介绍中国饮食，称去中国是“为了吃”，通过吃去理解。
items.statement_for_kb: The Guardian describes Fuchsia Dunlop as spending 30 years introducing Western audiences to Chinese food, saying she goes to China 'to eat' in order to understand.
items._pack_desc: 海外网站洋网红 / 外籍创作者图文

items.theme: Lost Plate overseas site: food reveals local stories
items.creator: Lost Plate Food Tours
items.title: Lost Plate Food Tours
items.quote_en: Food reveals things that the internet can't. Every dish has a story. It reflects local ingredients and preserves traditions that have been passed down for generations. A great food tour combines cuisine, culture, history, and neighborhood exploration into a single experience.
items.quote_cn: Lost Plate 官网：食物能揭示互联网看不到的东西；每道菜都有故事，连接食材、传统与街区生活。
items.statement_for_kb: Lost Plate's overseas website frames Chinese food tours as storytelling: each dish reflects local ingredients and generational traditions beyond what the internet shows.
items._pack_desc: 海外网站洋网红 / 外籍创作者图文
